entry_point.title: Bookstore API
entry_point.description:
A worked example exercising every construct the tree carries — including
**Markdown** in a description, which is what the RAML spec says every
`description:` is.

See [Getting started](#) for the `{tenant}` you will need.

type.name: tenant
type.description: The tenant subdomain

documentation.title: Getting started
documentation.content:
Every request goes to your own tenant, so the first thing to settle is
the `{tenant}` in the base URI: it is the subdomain you were given at
sign-up, and it is not optional.

    curl https://acme.books.example.com/v2/books

Reads of the catalogue are open. Anything that writes needs a token —
see **Authentication** below.

documentation.title: Authentication
documentation.content:
The API speaks OAuth 2.0. Send the caller to `/oauth/authorize`, exchange
the code at `/oauth/token`, and put the result in an `Authorization`
header:

    Authorization: Bearer <token>

Ask for the narrowest scopes that will do. `read:books` is enough to
list and retrieve; `write:books` is needed to add one; `admin:catalogue`
is for tools, not for applications.

`GET /books/{isbn}` may also be called with no token at all, which is
what the open padlock on that method means.

documentation.title: Pagination
documentation.content:
Collections are paged with `offset` and `limit`. `limit` defaults to 20
and is capped at 100; asking for more is not an error, it is quietly
reduced.

There is no cursor. Adding a book while you page can shift the window,
so a client walking the whole catalogue should sort and de-duplicate on
`isbn` rather than trusting the offsets.

documentation.title: Errors
documentation.content:
Failures use the status code and nothing else — there is no error
envelope to parse.

* `400` — the body did not match the schema on this page.
* `401` — no token, or one that has expired.
* `422` — the body was well-formed but matched no member of a union.
* `500` — ours. Retry with backoff; it is safe for every method here
  except `POST /books`, which is not idempotent.

Money.name: Money
Money.description: An amount and the currency it is denominated in.

Book.name: Book
Book.description:
One book in the catalogue.

A book is identified by its `isbn`, which is the *thirteen*-digit form
with no separators. Two fields are worth knowing about:

* `price` is the current price; `priceHistory` is every price it has
  had, oldest first.
* `related` is a list of other books, and may point back at this one.

The bounds a scale is allowed to be out by, written at the limits of a

documentation survived the trip.

machineToken.name: machineToken
machineToken.description:
Two-legged client credentials, for server-to-server callers that have no user
to send through a browser.

type.name: Authorization
type.description: The word Bearer, a space, then the access token.

type.name: access_token?
type.description:
The same token, for callers that cannot set a header (RFC 6750 § 2.3).
Prefer the header: a query string is logged by every proxy in between.

401.description: The token was missing, expired, or issued to another client.

basic.name: basic
basic.description: Username and password, for server-to-server callers only.

type.name: Authorization
type.description: The word Basic, a space, then base64(user:password).
